To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the isotropic shifts in paramagnetic molecules are temperature independent in the'solid state' and in the 'liquid state' and that the temperature dependence of correlation times cannot be the origin of non-Curie behavior.

the isotropic chemical shift in paramagnetic molecules in liquids and in the solid state is independent of the correlation time and hence of the temperature, and that the temperature dependence is due to a change in the electronic relaxation time, which is the same for both states.
The isotropic shift is independent of the molecular tumbling time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electronic structure of paramagnetic compounds.
the study of the magnetic resonance of nuclei in molecules.
the development of new methods of analysis for the characterization of materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the isotropie shift is a property of the electronic system, and is therefore not a property of the molecular motion, but of the electronic spin system.
the observed temperature dependence of the isotropie nmr shifts in paramagnetic molecules cannot be explained by the theory of the isotropic chemical shifts.
the isotropic chemical shift is a measure of the electronic spin density at the nucleus and is independent of the molecular motions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in paramagnetic systems the temperature dependence of nmr shifts is determined by the temperature dependence of molecular motions, whereas the absolute values of the shifts are determined by the electronic structure.
in the case of free rotation of the molecule, the temperature dependence is determined by the Curie law, and in the case of slow rotation, by the Curie-Weiss law.
the isotropic chemical shift is a measure of the electronic spin density in the molecular framework.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isotropic shifts of paramagnetic molecules in solution should be independent of the relative magnitude of the correlation time and the electronic spin relaxation time.
the isotropic NMR shifts of paramagnetic compounds can be used to study the dynamics of the molecules in solution, even when the molecules tumble slowly.
the isotropic NMR shifts in liquids are independent of the relative magnitude of the tumbling times and electronic relaxation times.
